correctness.rationale: The enhanced invariant preserves incidence and sorts as well as collinearity/concurrency of same-sort triples. With at most three stationary vertices, repeats reduce to ≤2 distinct anchors. A same-sort triple is governed by its pair-lines or common line; for three collinear points a fresh point on their line has q−2 choices and a line avoiding them has q(q−2) choices. For three noncollinear points there are (q−1)² points off all pair-lines and (q−1)² lines avoiding the anchors. For a mixed triple A,B,L, the two relevant lines for a new point are AB and L, whose intersection is old, fresh, or the whole common line as dictated by I(A,L), I(B,L). A candidate new line is classified by its incidences with A,B and equality with L; only the unique line through both can be exhausted by L for q≥3. The dual cases exhaust the other sorts. These counts are uniform at q=2 as well when their zero cases are removed, so any two order-two planes also have matching profiles. With two anchors all atomic cases are already available at q=2; these permanent strategies prove the unrestricted-depth bounds. The four-name separator asks for three distinct concurrent lines plus a point off their union, using a local rebind of the point name. There are exactly q(q−2) points off any such triple of lines; thus it separates the orders as stated.
